questions.question: With renderToPipeableStream, what is the 'shell'?
options: Everything outside the nearest Suspense boundaries, sent as soon as it is ready
The fallback shown when the server crashes
questions.explanation: The shell is the part of the tree not wrapped in a Suspense boundary. onShellReady fires when it can be sent; suspended parts stream in later.

questions.question: What does hydration do?
options: Attaches event handlers and React state to existing server-rendered DOM without recreating it
Re-renders the page on the server
Deletes the server HTML and renders from scratch
questions.explanation: hydrateRoot renders the same tree in the browser and adopts the existing DOM nodes, making the page interactive.

questions.question: Which of these will cause a hydration mismatch?
options: Using useId to generate an element id
Setting state inside useEffect after mount
questions.explanation: Math.random() produces different output on server and client, so the first client render won't match the server HTML.

questions.question: A user clicks inside a Suspense boundary that has not hydrated yet. What does React do?
options: Prioritises hydrating that boundary first (selective hydration)
Falls back to client rendering the whole app
questions.explanation: With streaming SSR, boundaries hydrate independently, and React raises the priority of the boundary the user is interacting with.
